key_insight: In a small proof-of-concept study, GPT-5 reconstructed pregnancy episodes from clinical notes more completely and with more accurate dates than an ICD-code algorithm.
clinical_relevance: Narrative-based extraction could complement billing codes for maternal and fetal health research by capturing pregnancies and details missing from structured data.
method: Provided GPT-5 with chronologically concatenated clinical notes and messages.
Extracted pregnancy episodes, dates, outcomes, reproductive treatments, and complications.
Compared results with manual chart review and a hierarchical ICD-code algorithm.
evidence_signal: Among 20 held-out patients with 54 pregnancies, GPT-5 detected 53 versus 40 for the code algorithm, with 3 versus 24 spurious episodes and F1 scores of 0.96 versus 0.68.
watch_item: Different input sources prevent attributing gains solely to the LLM; validation in larger, multi-institutional cohorts is needed.
paper_title: Beyond billing codes: a proof-of-concept study of large language models for pregnancy episode reconstruction from clinical notes
